outlook.statement: Vardhman Holdings Limited primarily earns its income from investments. The Company's strategy is to adopt a systematic approach of investment into different asset classes namely debt, equity & real estate and to keep the portfolio dynamic as per the changing market conditions.
The Company is evaluating the impact of Ind AS 118, Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements, effective for annual periods beginning on or after April 1, 2027, on its financial statements.

Ind AS 118, Presentation and Disclosure in Financial Statements, has been issued by ICAI and is effective for annual periods beginning on or after April 1, 2027. The Company is evaluating the impact of the Standard on its financial statements.

risks: The Company is a NBFC registered with RBI and mainly engaged in investment activities. It follows a strategy of adopting a systematic approach to investment into different asset classes and keeping the portfolio dynamic as per the changing market conditions. The Company is prone to all the financial risks and capital market fluctuations.
Uncertainty in recovery of investment value from IL&FS group
Claims/litigations from various parties in ordinary course of business

Market Risk: Currency Risk (currently no foreign currency transactions, hence not exposed), Interest Rate Risk (no significant floating rate assets/liabilities, no significant impact), Price Risk (exposed from investments classified at FVTPL and FVOCI; managed via diversification, strategic asset allocation benchmarks and risk limits)

Credit Risk: Maximum exposure Rs 286.19 crore (Mar 2026) and Rs 258.96 crore (Mar 2025); receivables immaterial; creditworthiness evaluated on ongoing basis; investments made after considering counterparty risks (Tier I capital, CAR, credit rating, profitability, NPA levels, deposit base); all investments fair valued and receivables/bank balances/other financial assets considered good

Liquidity Risk: No borrowings; other financial liabilities negligible (Rs 7.25 lakh Mar 2026, Rs 7.00 lakh Mar 2025); principal liquidity sources are cash/cash equivalents and operating cash flows; surplus funds invested ensuring liquidity availability; negligible liquidity risk
Market risk arising from investments held at fair value through profit or loss or other comprehensive income (price risk)
Uncertainty regarding recovery of investment value from IL&FS group companies (preference shares measured at nil value)
Market risk: changes in prices of investments
Credit risk: risk of financial loss if customer or counter-party fails to meet contractual obligations
Liquidity risk: risk that the Company will not be able to meet its financial obligations as and when they become due
Investment risk: actual return on plan assets below expected return will create plan deficit
Salary risk: deviation in rate of increase in salary from assumed rate
Interest risk: fall in interest rates will increase the ultimate cost of providing benefit
Longevity risk: increase in life expectancy of plan participants will increase plan's liability
